Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.

Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description says that, while several parallel activities run for the same case, one actor also performs a separate action that is not part of those activities, and the later step must wait for this action as well.: Model that separate action as its own task on a dedicated parallel branch that starts at the same parallel gateway as the other parallel activities. Rejoin all branches at one parallel gateway before the later step that depends on them. Do not fold the action into another task or into the task that precedes the split, and do not omit it.

When the description states that one branch or outcome of a decision is followed by several separately named actions performed by different actors or departments (for example, one actor receives materials while another department sets something up), joined by 'and' or 'and also': Model each separately named action as its own task in that branch, with one task per actor action, and do not merge them into one task, even when the actions are described in the same sentence. Place the tasks in parallel after the branch's split, and join them with a parallel gateway when the description requires all of them to be completed before the process continues.

When the description states, in one sentence, that one actor performs two distinct actions joined by 'and': Model each of the two actions as its own task, labeled with the action the description names, in the order the description gives, connected by a sequence flow. Do not combine them into a single task, even when the actions are closely related or the label of one of them is a broad summary.

When the description names two separately stated activities of the same actor, joined by 'and' under one verb phrase (for example, conducting one kind of study and another kind of study): Model each named activity as its own task, in the order the description gives, connected by sequence flows. Do not merge them into one task that carries the combined name.
